newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary sees crawling forint devaluation till 1999.
newsitem.headline: Hungary sees crawling forint devaluation till 1999.

text.p: Hungary's finance minister Peter Medgyessy said on Monday the monthly crawling peg devaluation of the forint will continue until at least 1999.
"The crawling peg devaluation can only be abolished if inflation falls to single digits," he told reporters.
"I believe inflation can decrease by five percent annually in the next two to three years. This means that inflation can become single-digit by 1999, or rather 2000," Medgyessy said.
The crawling peg devaluation was introduced as part of the government's austerity package of March 1995 as a means of devaluing the then overvalued forint in a controlled and predictable way.

The devaluation was initially fixed at 1.3 percent per month and reduced to 1.2 percent per month in January this year. Last month National Bank of Hungary head Gyorgy Suranyi announced the rate would stay at a maximum 1.2 percent for 1997.
Medgyessy said on Monday such a rate had not yet been decided.
"It needs a another decision by the government," he said. "But 1.2 percent is likely."
